correctness.rationale: Finite graph model is explicit: 18 primitive incidences, 1,727 nonempty faces, f-vector (18,126,428,705,450), binary boundary ranks (17,109,319,386). Acyclicity is checked by the finite functional successor graph. The rational-rank upper bounds from boundary composition force equality with the mod-two ranks, hence fourth integral homology is a free lattice of rank 64. Direct signed fixed-face counting gives layer-swap trace -4, hence rational eigenspace dimensions (30,34). Exact binary top-cycle elimination gives rank 30 for tau-I; independently rank([boundary4;I+tau])=416 versus rank(boundary4)=386. The universal coefficient injection identifies reduction of the free top homology with the entire 64-dimensional F2 homology. An explicit integral involution lemma then forces 30 regular and four sign summands. The actual embedded verifier completes in standard Python and reproduces each finite invariant; no experimental extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The triangular prism is the smallest nontrivial closed prism graph and a canonical cubic test for ordinary discrete Morse complexes. Classifying the complete integral action of its geometric layer exchange is a natural exact topological invariant, not a parameter-selected slice. The 30 regular integral blocks constitute genuinely nonsplit integral extension information invisible to the known rational character or 64-sphere homotopy type: 30 rational invariant dimensions exist but no trivial integral direct summand. This concrete integral representation is reusable in studying transfer and local-coefficient/equivariant constructions for this natural action; no downstream theorem or broader classification is asserted.
